package.name: apify
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Two nodes, one token.
#
# THE LAST HALF OF THE OLD `crawl` PACKAGE. Its three Hyperbrowser nodes became
# `nodes/hyperbrowser/`; these two are Apify, which shares no endpoint, credential or shape
# with them and was only ever in the same package because both are "web scraping".
#
# I RECORDED THIS PACKAGE AS UNMIGRATABLE ONCE, and that was wrong twice over. The claim was
# that ApifyResults is a stateful iterator, so computation. Reading it properly:
#
#   1. The iterator is DEAD. It emits one item per `continue` signal and declares that input
#      via `getTriggerInputs()`, a hook that exists in NO base class any more — not in
#      plugin-base, not in the engine's CallbackNode. Only two nodes in the tree override
#      it and nothing calls it. So the node fetches the list, emits item[0], and waits for a
#      signal that is never routed.
#
#   2. Iterating is not this node's job. LoopStart/LoopEnd own it, in the marketplace
#      `flow` package, and LOOP_NODES_SPEC.md names the self-continuing CallbackNode as the
#      exact design they replaced. So ApifyResults returns the whole list and a canvas that
#      wants one at a time wires a loop, which is the platform's answer rather than this
#      node's re-invention of it.
#
# The real gaps were two small capabilities, both now built: `offset` pagination, and
# `sha256` in the expression sandbox for the content ids.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/crawl/`.

name: apify
displayName: Apify
description: Run Apify actors and tasks, and read their results
version: 1.0.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751511484/gravity/icons/apifyLogo.png

features:
  - Start an actor or a saved task from a list of URLs
  - Read a finished run's dataset, following every page
  - Stable universal and content ids for dedup

allowedHosts:
  - api.apify.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  # The dataset endpoint counts ROWS, not pages, so the walk steps by the page size.
  paginate: [offset]
  # ApifyStarter follows the run when asked to wait for it.
  poll: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.1.0"

credentials.apifyCredential.yaml:
# Transcribed from the retired crawl/src/credentials/index.ts, NAME AND FIELD UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `apifyCredential` keep resolving after the move. Note
# the field is `token`, not `apiKey`: Apify calls it a token and the stored rows say token.

name: apifyCredential
displayName: Apify
description: Apify API credentials for starting actor runs and reading their results
documentationUrl: https://docs.apify.com/api/v2

properties:
  - name: token
    displayName: API Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apify API token from console.apify.com
    placeholder: ""

shared.apify.yaml:
# What both nodes share: how to reach Apify, and how a URL list is read.

call: &call
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.apifyCredential.token }}"
  headers:
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# THE URL LIST, normalised. The panel's field is a template that usually carries a JSON
# array as a STRING, and an upstream node may hand over a real array instead.
#
# ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE from the retired parseUrls: a string that opens with `[` and
# fails to parse THROWS rather than being treated as a single URL. The sandbox has no
# try/catch, and the retired node was inconsistent with itself anyway — its own validation
# rejected unparseable JSON with "URLs must be a valid JSON array" while the service it
# called fell back to scraping the broken string. One of those had to go, and the error is
# the honest one.
urls: &urls >-
  return Array.isArray(config.urls)
    ? config.urls.map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
    : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim().startsWith('[')
      ? JSON.parse(config.urls.trim()).map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
      : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim()
        ? [config.urls.trim()]
        : []

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# THE SANITISE STEP IS TRANSCRIBED, NOT DROPPED, because it is the part of this node that
# other things depend on:
#
#   crawl / metadata.headers  removed. They are large and they are per-fetch noise. The
#                             retired node stripped them because a full crawl payload
#                             through the bus caused JSON parsing failures downstream.
#   universalId               sha256(url), 12 hex. The join key for dedup and ref hydration.
#   contentId                 sha256 over url + text + the metadata that identifies a page.
#                             Two fetches of an unchanged page give the same contentId, and
#                             that is what makes "have I already seen this?" answerable.
#
# Both ids need a hash, which is why `sha256` is now in the expression sandbox. It is a
# pure function of its argument, so it meets the same bar as encodeURIComponent: the
# alternative was keeping this whole node in TypeScript for one line of arithmetic.

- emit: items
  from: response
  value: >-
    return (((response || {}).items) || []).map(it => Object.assign(
      Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(it).filter(e => e[0] !== 'crawl' && e[0] !== 'metadata')),
      it.metadata
        ? { metadata: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(it.metadata).filter(e => e[0] !== 'headers')) }
        : {},
      it.url ? { universalId: sha256(it.url).substring(0, 12) } : {},
      [it.url, it.text, (it.metadata || {}).title, (it.metadata || {}).description,
       (it.metadata || {}).canonicalUrl, (it.metadata || {}).author,
       (it.metadata || {}).keywords, (it.metadata || {}).languageCode]
        .concat(Array.isArray((it.metadata || {}).openGraph)
          ? it.metadata.openGraph.map(og => og.content)
          : [])
        .filter(Boolean).length
        ? { contentId: sha256(
            [it.url, it.text, (it.metadata || {}).title, (it.metadata || {}).description,
             (it.metadata || {}).canonicalUrl, (it.metadata || {}).author,
             (it.metadata || {}).keywords, (it.metadata || {}).languageCode]
              .concat(Array.isArray((it.metadata || {}).openGraph)
                ? it.metadata.openGraph.map(og => og.content)
                : [])
              .filter(Boolean).join('|')
          ).substring(0, 12) }
        : {}
    ))

# The count of what actually came back, across every page of the walk. Not a config bound
# and not the first page's length.
- emit: total
  from: response
  value: "return (((response || {}).items) || []).length"
files.api/run.yaml:
# TWO CALLS, because a run does not hold its own data.
#
# The run record names a dataset, and the dataset holds the items, so reading a run is a
# lookup and then a walk. This is the case the whole `run` list exists for: the second
# URL is built from the first reply.

- $ref: apify#call
  name: run
  method: GET
  url: "return 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/' + config.runId"

  # A run with no dataset is a real state (an actor that produced nothing), and it is worth
  # catching HERE rather than letting the next URL be built with `undefined` in it.
  error:
    when: "return !((response.data || {}).defaultDatasetId)"
    message: >-
      return 'this run has no dataset to read (status '
        + ((response.data || {}).status || 'unknown') + ')'

# OFFSET PAGINATION. Apify's dataset endpoint counts ROWS, so the walk steps by the page
# size rather than by 1, which is why `offset` is its own strategy and not `page`.
#
# 1000 is Apify's own maximum per request, and it is the STEP as well as the size.
- $ref: apify#call
  name: items
  method: GET
  url: "return 'https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets/' + calls.run.data.defaultDatasetId + '/items'"

  paginate:
    strategy: offset
    into: offset
    size: 1000
    # This endpoint returns a BARE ARRAY, not an object with a rows key.
    items: "return Array.isArray(response) ? response : []"

  query:
    limit: "1000"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [runId]
  properties:
    runId:
      type: string
      title: Run ID
      description: The Apify run to read. Comes from Apify Starter's runId output.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [runId]
files.interface.yaml:
# NO `continue` INPUT, and no item/index/hasMore outputs. Those belonged to the iterator
# this node no longer is; see node.yaml for why. A canvas that wants one item at a time
# wires Loop Start to `items`, which is the platform's own mechanism.

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: string
    description: The Apify run id to read results from
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: items
    type: array
    description: >-
      Every item in the run's dataset, each with a universalId derived from its url and a
      contentId derived from its content.
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many items the run produced

credentials:
  - name: apifyCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Apify API
files.node.yaml:
type: ApifyResults
kind: PromiseNode

name: Apify Results
category: Web Scraping
color: "#00B4A6"

# A PromiseNode NOW, where the retired one was a CallbackNode. That is the substantive
# change in this migration and it is a correction, not a downgrade.
#
# The old node emitted ONE item per `continue` signal and declared that input through
# `getTriggerInputs()`. No base class implements that hook any more, in plugin-base or in
# the engine, and nothing calls it: the node fetched the list, emitted item[0], and waited
# for a signal nothing routed.
#
# Iterating is also not this node's job. LoopStart and LoopEnd own it — they live in the
# marketplace `flow` package now, having been retired from core — and LOOP_NODES_SPEC.md
# names the self-continuing CallbackNode as the design they replaced. So this reads the run
# and hands back the whole list; a canvas that wants one item at a time wires a loop, which
# is one mechanism for every collection rather than one re-invented per node.

description: Read every item a finished Apify run produced

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to read what an Apify run scraped. Always the downstream half of Apify Starter: feed
  it the run id. It returns every item in the run's dataset, following each page, with a
  stable id per item. To handle them one at a time, wire Loop Start to the items.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A finished run's dataset is immutable, so the same run id genuinely gives the same
  # items and a prior output may be reused (EXECUTION_EFFICIENCY.md §3.2).
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
# NEEDS A REAL RUN ID. Apify runs are per-account, so there is no public fixture to point
# at; replace runId with one from your own console before running this.

testData:
  config:
    runId: REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_RUN_ID
  inputs:
    signal: REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_RUN_ID
  expect:
    # The ids are the reason this node is more than a fetch, so they are what is asserted.
    # Checked by LENGTH and alphabet rather than a regex: the expression sandbox rejects a
    # regex literal on purpose, so an assertion cannot smuggle one in either.
    items: >-
      return Array.isArray(output.items) && output.items.length > 0
        && output.items.filter(i => i.url).every(i =>
             typeof i.universalId === 'string' && i.universalId.length === 12
             && i.universalId.split('').every(c => '0123456789abcdef'.includes(c)))
        && output.items.every(i => i.crawl === undefined)
    total: "return output.total === output.items.length"
